findings.title: Specific client resource blocks all-clients fallback
findings.body: hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) only evaluates the all-clients resource when no resource named with that client id exists. If any permission was already created for that client (for example map-roles only), the client resource is found and evaluation stops there. A broader Clients-type grant such as view or manage all clients is never consulted, so that client is denied a scope the caller was granted for every client. The same method also calls PolicyStore.findByResource with the result of getResourceTypeResource without a null check; if the "Clients" type resource is missing, that path throws NullPointerException instead of denying.

findings.title: Map-roles checks ignore manage-clients and manage
findings.body: canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles, and canMapClientScopeRoles return only hasPermission for the matching scope. They do not treat AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS or canManage(client) as sufficient, unlike the V1 client permission evaluator and unlike canManage/canConfigure in this same class. A realm administrator who has manage-clients (or an FGAP manage grant) can update the client but is forbidden from mapping its roles, composites, or client-scope roles unless a separate map-roles permission exists.

findings.title: Schema init does not migrate existing admin-permissions clients
findings.body: init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already set, and only then creates scopes and the per-type resources. Realms that already initialized fine-grained admin permissions for Users never receive the Clients resource type or the new configure, map-roles-client-scope, and map-roles-composite scopes. Client permission creation then fails scope validation, and evaluation of all-clients permissions cannot find the type resource.

findings.title: Client permission resources have no display name
findings.body: getResourceName resolves Users resources to a username (or "All users") but has no Clients branch. Client resources are stored under the client UUID with no display name, so the admin API falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is null. Permission listings for the new Clients type show a blank name instead of the clientId or "All clients".

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission returns type name, not client ids
findings.body: getClientsWithPermission walks every resource of type Clients and adds resource.getName() when the scope is granted. The all-clients resource is also type Clients and is named "Clients", so an all-clients grant puts the literal "Clients" into the result instead of every client id. Callers that filter the client list by this set will not include the actual clients, and a per-client grant is not combined with the type-level grant.
